spec.title: Fix TreeDataProvider getParent method for find task reveal
spec.context: The Find Task command in the VSCode extension throws an error when selecting a task from the quick pick. VSCode's TreeView.reveal() API requires the TreeDataProvider to implement a getParent() method to traverse the tree hierarchy and locate the item to reveal. Currently, the tasks-view capability's TreeDataProvider does not implement this method.

in-scope.item: Implement getParent() method in tasks-view TreeDataProvider
Track parent relationships for TaskItem, ActionItem, and FileItem
Enable reveal() to work for finding and highlighting tasks

out-of-scope.item: Changes to the Find Task QuickPick UI
Adding reveal functionality to other tree views

requirements.requirement: The TreeDataProvider shall implement a getParent(element) method that returns the parent TreeItem for any given element
When getParent is called with a StatusGroupItem, it shall return undefined (root level)
When getParent is called with a TaskItem, it shall return the parent StatusGroupItem
When getParent is called with an ActionItem or FileItem, it shall return the parent TaskItem
The getParent implementation shall use cached TreeItem instances to ensure reveal() receives the same object references returned by getChildren()

files.file: Add getParent() method to TreeDataProvider and implement parent tracking using Maps

pattern.name: TreeItem caching
pattern.description: Existing pattern uses Maps to cache StatusGroupItems and TaskItems for reveal() compatibility

pattern.name: Capability mechanism pattern
pattern.description: Capabilities handle I/O and VSCode API interactions without policy decisions

product.finding: Find Task workflow: QuickPick opens, user selects task, task should be revealed and highlighted in TreeView. Currently fails with getParent error.

engineering.finding: Tasks-view capability defines TreeItem types: StatusGroupItem, TaskItem, ActionItem, FileItem. Uses factory-di pattern with dependency injection.

codebase.finding: TreeDataProvider at lines 266-289 implements getTreeItem and getChildren but not getParent
reveal() is called at extension.ts:366-367 with statusGroup and taskItem
Existing caching uses cachedStatusGroups array and cachedTaskItems Map

pitfalls.finding: getParent must return the exact same object instance that getChildren returned, otherwise reveal() will fail to match elements
ActionItem and FileItem are created fresh in getChildrenForTask(), need to cache these or track their parent differently
Cache must be cleared on refresh to avoid stale parent references

constraints.constraint: Must use same cached instances for parent lookup that getChildren() returns
Must follow capability pattern - no policy logic, only mechanism
Must clear parent tracking on tree refresh

internal.dependency: VSCode TreeDataProvider API - getParent is optional but required for reveal()

risk.mitigation: Use Maps keyed by task ID and status, clear on refresh

risks.risk: Parent cache could become stale if not properly invalidated on refresh
